content.text:
I submitted index 24 (Cu 0.135, Sb 0.865) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.00286 %, the highest of the three I measured, but every value on this Cu–Sb oxide line was very low.

| Index | Cu fraction | EQE (%) | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.674 | 0.000069 | Tests the Cu-rich half of the line |
| 15 | 0.346 | 0.00041 | Nearest to CuSb2O6, the one stable Cu–Sb oxide |
| 24 | 0.135 | 0.00286 | Sb-rich end, following the rising trend |

- **Trend:** EQE went up steadily as Sb content increased, about 40× from index 5 to index 24.
- **Stability model (MACE):** CuSb2O6 sits on the stability hull, so index 15 should be close to pure CuSb2O6. Cu2SbO5 is far above the hull (1.16 eV/atom), so the Cu-rich side is probably a CuO + CuSb2O6 mixture.
- **Band-gap model (MEGNet):** I didn't trust it here. It gave about 0 eV for CuSb2O6, whose measured gap is around 2 eV.

**Limits:**
- With only three measurements the peak may not be at index 24. Indices 25–29 are even more Sb-rich, were never measured and could score higher.
- The composition range between the points I measured is also untested.
- I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase assignments above come from the stability model, not from diffraction.
